Pine
pīn
n., v. (a tree; also to waste away; rendering Hebrew tidhar and maqaq)
From Latin pinus for the tree; the verb is a separate Old English word meaning to torment or waste. The KJV uses both.

Biblical Definition

Pine names a tree and an action. Isaiah lists it among the timbers brought to beautify the sanctuary: “The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary” (Isa 60:13). The verb means to waste away: Ezekiel's exiles “pine away for their iniquity” (Eze 24:23), and Lamentations describes those who “pine away, stricken through for want of the fruits of the field” (Lam 4:9).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines pine as a tree of the genus Pinus; and as a verb, to languish, to lose flesh or wear away under any distress or anxiety of mind.

expand to see more

PINE, n. A tree of the genus Pinus, of many species.

PINE, v.i. To languish; to lose flesh or wear away under any distress or anxiety of mind.

2. To languish with desire; to waste away with longing for something.

Key Scripture

Isa 60:13 — "The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious."

Eze 24:23 — "And your tires shall be upon your heads, and your shoes upon your feet: ye shall not mourn nor weep; but ye shall pine away for your iniquities, and mourn one toward another."

Lam 4:9 — "They that be slain with the sword are better than they that be slain with hunger: for these pine away, stricken through for want of the fruits of the field."

Eze 33:10 — "Therefore, O thou son of man, speak unto the house of Israel; Thus ye speak, saying, If our transgressions and our sins be upon us, and we pine away in them, how should we then live?"

Modern Corruption

Unconfessed guilt is expected to fade with time, and Ezekiel describes exiles pining away under it until the word of the LORD comes to them.

expand to see more

Ezekiel 33:10 records the exiles' own diagnosis: if our transgressions and our sins be upon us, and we pine away in them, how should we then live? They were not defiant; they were wasting. And God's answer refuses both despair and denial: as I live, saith the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live. Guilt does not evaporate with time, but it is not the final word either — there is a turning offered, and the invitation comes from the offended party.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew tidhar (H8410), a pine or elm; maqaq (H4743), to melt or pine away; dub (H1727), to languish.

expand to see more

Hebrew tidhar (H8410) — pine tree; Isaiah 41:19, 60:13.

Hebrew maqaq (H4743) — to pine away, rot; Ezekiel 24:23, 33:10, Leviticus 26:39.

Usage

"“The fir tree, the pine tree, and the box… to beautify… my sanctuary” — timber brought to worship."

"“Ye shall pine away for your iniquities” — guilt that does not fade."

"“How should we then live?” — the exiles' question, and God's answer."
